what_it_does: Chiplets communicate through wires on the same silicon die, and to pack more data through fewer wires, engineers send signals in both directions at the same time on a single wire (simultaneous bidirectional signaling). This creates interference problems: your own transmitter's signal bounces back as an echo, and nearby wires interfere with each other (crosstalk). This design solves all three using analog cancellation circuits built into the transceiver—canceling out the echo from your own transmitter, canceling signals bleeding in from neighboring wires, and removing the ground shielding that would normally protect the wires but wastes space. The result is extremely dense, high-speed communication for modern chiplet interfaces.
